Subject: Staged Eval Playbook: retention & compliance clarifications for MPA (SOC 2 / SIG / DPA)

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for taking a call yesterday — great alignment on scope. As discussed, we want to put a short staged evaluation playbook into the MPA so your procurement and security teams have a clear acceptance path. Attached are the three artifacts we typically share as part of the MAP intake: a one-page SOC 2 Type II summary, our completed SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet, and a draft DPA with the most common redlines pre-populated.

A few clarifying questions from our side so we can lock timelines into the MAP: 
- Retention window: do you need a single 7-year archival clause, or are there mixed requirements by dataset type (transactional vs. ML features)?
- Data residency: Procurement flagged EU residency for any records derived from EU customers — is Starlend expecting a hard requirement in the DPA or a plan to enable EU-residency within 90 days of go-live?
- SIG items: Please highlight any "must-have" rows in column H of the SIG sheet; we will triage remediation or compensating controls in the MAP.

Proposed next steps: We can provision the evaluation tenant and a short test plan by 12/15 if legal and security sign off on the DPA redlines and retention carveouts. If that timeline works, Kimberly will coordinate the evidence handoff and Neha will own the SOC2 walk-through.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the priority items you want in the MAP.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_type2_summary_2026.pdf (summary), SIG_CA_IQ_answers_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed_DPA_redlines_starlend_20261208.docx (tracked-redline)
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@starlend.com>

Cc: Legal Team <legal@starlend.com>, Jim Blake <jim.blake@starlend.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged Eval Playbook: retention & compliance clarifications for MPA (SOC 2 / SIG / DPA)

Markus — thanks for the materials. Quick answers up-front: 
- Retention: for regulatory reporting we need transaction-level records retained for 7 years; non-PII telemetry can be 2 years. We can provide a table for the MAP showing which dataset maps to which retention bucket.
- Data residency: our initial requirement is that any production-stored EU customer data must be resident in EU regions. For the evaluation we can accept a plan that binds you to enable EU residency within 90 days of production rollout.
- SIG: I’ll flag must-haves in the sheet by EOD.

Timing: Legal needs the redline DPA reviewed; if Redwood’s proposed redlines are narrow we can push procurement to sign the MAP by 12/20 and start the eval the week of 12/22. If there are material DPA changes we’ll need a week for review.

I’ve cc’d our legal lead and Jim (CTO) to the loop.

Cheers,
Alice Turner
Director, Platform Partnerships
Starlend

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick reply. A few operational notes to make the MAP explicit: 

1) Retention matrix: I’ve sketched the matrix we usually include in MAPs — transactional (7y), account metadata (5y), derived embeddings/ML features (90d by default, longer if specifically required), and logs/telemetry (2y). I’ll attach the matrix as a Sheet and add a column for Starlend’s required exceptions.

2) EU residency: we can add a milestone in the MAP: "EU-residency enablement - ETA 90 days post-prod", and a fallback where we limit EU-derived data to pseudonymized KMS-protected blobs during the eval. That can be a gating condition for production acceptance.

3) DPA redlines: Marked up the clauses we expect to see negotiated: subprocessor list, breach notification SLA (24h), data subject request handling, and export controls. We do not anticipate wholesale changes to liability caps, but we are open to a CRO-level conversation if Starlend requires higher limits for a subset of regulated data.

I’ve attached an updated DPA with comments (proposed_DPA_redlines_starlend_20261208.docx) and the SIG answers with the "must-have" column highlighted.

If procurement and legal can confirm the retention buckets and the narrow DPA points above by 12/17, we’ll commit to provisioning the eval by 12/22.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Hi all — adding operational detail on the eval tenant and data handling: 

- Eval data: We recommend synthetic or anonymized slices for the evaluation tenant. If Starlend prefers a copy of production, we require a data transfer playbook and explicit sign-off in the MAP; that will also trigger additional SOC2 evidence requests.
- Archival: For any dataset designated to the 7-year bucket, we will move data to cold storage and apply immutable retention controls; this is separate from log/telemetry retention. The MAP will include an Acceptance Milestone: "Retention configuration validated by Starlend security via provided test artifacts".
- EU residency plan: We will add a rollout milestone and an acceptance check (demo of EU-region data locality with synthetic test records) — ETA 90 days post-prod.

Next steps: Markus will collect Starlend’s retention table and legal comments so we can finalize the MAP and schedule the DPA review call (12/13 optional).

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
